jobs.description_text: About the Role We're looking for a software engineer, reliability-minded but still a builder, to own what happens in production to the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. The platform team builds the manifest-driven API and controllers that let the inference team declare what they need, a cluster, a model deployment, a capacity change, and get it reconciled underneath. Your job is to keep that promise true in the real world: triaging InfiniBand issues when prefill and decode nodes stall exchanging KV cache over RDMA, diagnosing hero-model and LoRA-serving faults that don't show up in generic health checks, and extending the automated self-healing system so each new failure mode becomes a permanent fix instead of a recurring page. The core value we're after is keeping the decoupling real even when things break, and keeping the fleet efficient without that efficiency becoming a new source of instability. You'll own SLOs and error budgets for inference serving, lead incident response, and turn what postmortems teach you into actual changes in the controllers and automation, not just updated runbooks. You'll also work the reliability side of capacity efficiency, since a mistuned defragmentation or bin-packing pass is itself a production risk. We will do this through compelling graphical explanations; urgent, immersive field reporting in photography and video; sharp visual news coverage; and investigations driven by deep reporting on imagery and data. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE: Every launch starts with a question: will it hold? As a Dynamics & Structural Analyst at Rocket Lab, you'll answer it. Using modelling, simulation, and real flight data, you'll predict the violent vibration, shock, and loads that Electron endures from the pad to orbit and prove our structures can take it. From FEA that optimises dynamic response to post-processing flight data that validates every prediction, your analysis is what turns bold designs into reliable launch vehicles. As part of the Electron team, you will contribute to the analysis, design validation and future improvements of Electron vehicles, while also supporting launch operations, ground systems, and propulsion development. If it flies, you helped prove it could. WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO: Perform prediction of launch vehicle modal and vibration environments based on finite element analysis, analytical methods and real flight data. Contribute to test plan definition of components (such as electronics) and assemblies, support test activities and interpret test results for dynamic testing (random vibration, acoustics, shock) Define, process and interpret static and dynamic ground test and flight data using statistical and analytical methods, following closely to industry standards (Random Vibration, Shock, Quasi-Static, Acoustic). Working closely with avionics, mechanical, fluids and propulsion team members to ensure the components, structures and assemblies survive the harsh test and flight loads.

For avionics, assess component conformity, soldering quality, and conformal coating. Enter serial, batch, and lot numbers into our ERP system, review inspection records, and keep documentation accurate and correctly filed. The Marketplace Quality Engineering team exists to make sure our platform is buying the right impressions, not just more impressions. We own the systems that assess, measure, and optimize supply quality across the programmatic ecosystem. Our work spans deduplication, supply path analysis, quality modeling, and the tooling that turns those signals into decisions at bid time. The problems are technically deep — think identity resolution across fragmented supply chains, statistical modeling to separate signal from noise, and real-time decisioning at platform scale — and they have direct, measurable impact on both advertiser outcomes and platform economics. This is not theoretical work. When we ship a model update, spend distribution across the platform shifts. Our engineering decisions translate directly into tens of millions of dollars of measurable business impact. If you want to build systems where what you ship visibly matters, this is the team. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Pacing & Experimentation
jobs.description_text: About the role Every campaign on our platform has a budget and a flight, and our pacing system decides in real time how to spend it against 20M queries per second. It has to bid the right amount on every impression, at the right rate, so advertisers spend their budget in full and get the most value from it. Changing a system like that safely is its own engineering problem. An ordinary A/B traffic split breaks down here, because both arms draw on the same campaign budget and one arm's spend distorts the other. We solve this with budget split experiments: each arm gets its own share of the budget, its own pacing calculation and its own spend tracking, all inside one live campaign. This is now how we gain confidence in any change to bidding behavior. We are looking for a senior engineer to work across both areas: the pacing engine itself, and the experimentation infrastructure that proves changes to it. You will build in the services that compute pacing instructions and apply them at bid time. You will also extend the experiment framework so teams across the company can launch a trustworthy experiment in hours instead of weeks. We work in a highly collaborative environment with a broad range of technologies, including .NET, Kafka, Kubernetes, Spark and Delta Lake. If you have built experimentation platforms or real-time decisioning systems outside ad tech, such as trading, payments or marketplace pricing, we want to hear from you. Develop custom CodeQL queries, Semgrep rules, and Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)-based detection signatures to codify newly discovered bug patterns and automate regression testing across software evaluations. Present vulnerability perspectives, risk assessments, and testing metrics to program managers, stakeholders, and intelligence community partners. jobs.description_text: About the role: Agents are becoming first-class users of the internet. They sign in, call APIs, deploy code, and act on behalf of people and teams. As an engineer on the Agent Auth and Identity team, you'll help answer those questions. You'll build the systems that let agents and people authenticate, delegate access, and act safely across Vercel and the services our customers connect to. This is foundational work: identity and authorization sit underneath everything we ship, and getting them right for agents will shape how modern software gets built. The scope is intentionally broad. You might spend one quarter designing how credentials are issued and scoped for autonomous agents, and the next building the developer-facing APIs and SDKs that make secure auth feel effortless. You'll own systems end-to-end, from design through long-term operation in production. We're looking for engineers who care deeply about security and developer experience in equal measure, enjoy working on problems without established playbooks, and want to define how trust works in an agentic world. The Languages and Runtimes team is making it the home for the rest of the application: APIs, background workers, AI agents, and the services that connect them. This past year we took Python on Vercel to general availability, launched Vercel Services so frontends and backends deploy together as one project, and, alongside our Compute team, helped bring always-on background workers to the platform. Our work spans the path from source code to a running process: tooling that understands an application’s structure, packages its dependencies, and runs it on Vercel, plus language runtimes, SDKs, private service-to-service communication, and production observability.
